title: Every review round is kept, required, and visible
summary: A binder is committed with a roundtable record, and the record proves exactly one thing: a fresh multi-provider review of these exact bytes exists. What it cannot show is the work behind it. The thirteen rounds that produced today's context-economy binder — what each round found, what was fixed, what execution refuted, and which provider returned nothing at all — lived nowhere until someone wrote them out by hand into a file no tool reads. This binder turns that history into a mechanism. The recorder gains a round mode that appends each round to a ledger beside the record; the commit and merge gates refuse a plan whose rounds are not committed with it; and Karta Watch shows, on the binder's own card, how many rounds it took and what each one said. Recording stays what it is — the ledger never stands in for a record, and the floor the recorder enforces does not move.
motivation: Recording is not enough: the record proves a review happened on these exact bytes and says nothing about the rounds that produced them, so a review history survives only when someone chooses to write it by hand.

included: scripts/roundtable/run_review.py — a new --round mode that appends one round (its hash, every provider's verdict or the reason it gave none, what was fixed, what was refuted) to .karta/roundtable/<key>.rounds.json, plus a --record that points at the ledger and refuses to file a record the ledger's last round did not review
.karta/roundtable/context-economy.rounds.json — the one hand-written ledger, normalized to the emitted shape with every value preserved, so one shape exists for the gate and the page to read
scripts/hooks/roundtable_gate.py — the binder-commit gate and the integration-merge gate additionally require the ledger, and its last round's hash, when .karta/roundtable.json carries ledger: true
scripts/validate_plugin.py and .karta/roundtable.json — the new ledger key allowed and type-checked in the same edit that turns it on for this repo
skills/karta-status/scripts/serve_status.py, its selftest_behaviours.txt anchor and both generated mirrors — a per-binder review block in the derived state and a review strip on the binder card
docs/how-to/roundtable.md, docs/how-to/karta-watch.md, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md — the three-step flow, the thirteen-round ledger read as a worked example, and the strip
excluded: no change to what --record enforces: min_providers, the panel normalization and the freshness hash are untouched, and a below-floor panel is still refused a record
the ledger never substitutes for the record: --check keys on <key>.json alone, and a target carrying only a ledger still fails it (proven by a negative control)

no effect on this binder's own delivery: the gate runs from ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/scripts/hooks/roundtable_gate.py — the main checkout, not a build worktree — so both the new switch and the new check stay inert until this branch lands on main

no VERSION bump, no release notes, no plugin manifest change — that is release work

work_items.title: Every review round is appended to a ledger the recorder keeps
work_items.summary: The recorder gains a round mode that appends each review round — the content it reviewed, what every provider said or why it said nothing, what was fixed and what was refuted — to a per-target ledger, and it refuses to file the final record unless the ledger's last round reviewed that same content.
work_items.contract: The recorder learns to keep a per-target history, and to refuse a record that history does not back. (1) THE NEW MODE. scripts/roundtable/run_review.py gains a fourth mutually-exclusive mode beside --record, --check and --self-test: `... | python3 scripts/roundtable/run_review.py --round --target <slug-or-branch> [--kind binder|branch] [--fixed "..."]... [--refuted "..."]... [--note "..."]`. It reads the same raw roundtable DispatchResult on stdin that --record reads and normalizes it with the existing normalize_panel; that function, validate_normalized, and the record shape are otherwise untouched. (2) THE LEDGER AND ITS PATH. It appends one round to .karta/roundtable/<key>.rounds.json, where <key>.json is the record key the target already resolves to — <slug>.rounds.json for a binder, branch-<tip-sha>.rounds.json for a branch. The ledger is a sibling of the record and never a substitute: --check keys on <key>.json alone and must keep ignoring the ledger, proven by a negative control (a target with a ledger and no record still fails --check, exit 1). (3) WHICH BYTES A ROUND RECORDS, and why not the staged ones. --round computes reviewed_hash exactly the way --record does — target_identity(root, target, kind) with no candidate bytes, so a binder hashes the WORKTREE file and a branch resolves its tip sha. It does not hash the staged blob, and the reason is structural rather than a preference: stdin already carries the panel, so there is no channel to feed staged bytes in, and a --round that hashed the index would disagree with the --record it must match whenever the working tree is dirty. The gate compares the ledger's last round against the staged blob exactly as it already compares the record, so in the only state that commits — worktree equal to index — all three agree, and when they differ both checks re-arm together. (4) THE ROUND SHAPE. Each appended round is an object with exactly these keys: round (1-based, one more than the rounds already there), reviewed_hash, run_at (UTC isoformat, as the record uses), providers, findings_fixed, findings_refuted_or_deferred, notes, below_floor. providers maps each panel entry's provider name to {model, verdict, status}: model from the raw entry's model field else null, verdict the normalized verdict else null, status the raw entry's status string else null. A provider that returned nothing is KEPT here with verdict null and its status — that is the point of the ledger, and the one place it differs from validate_normalized, which drops such an entry from the floor count. findings_fixed and findings_refuted_or_deferred are the --fixed and --refuted values in the order given (empty lists when none); notes is the --note value or the empty string. No panel prose is copied into a round: the full responses of the final round already live in the record, and thirteen copies of them is a payload Karta Watch would then carry on every poll. (5) THE FLOOR DOES NOT BLOCK A ROUND. A round below min_providers is still appended, carrying below_floor: true — it happened, and the ledger is history. --round refuses (exit 2, writing nothing) only for the two things that are not a round at all: a stdin payload normalize_panel rejects, and a target that cannot be resolved. On success it git-adds the ledger the way --record stages the record, and prints the path and the round number. (6) THE HEADER. When the ledger does not exist it is created with a header of target_ref, target_kind, tool (from the config, as the record does), agents (the {provider, model} list seen in this first round) and note — one plain sentence saying what the file is, that the gate's freshness check reads the sibling record, and that rounds are appended in order. A later append never rewrites the header and never drops a header key it did not write: a provider first seen in round 4 appears in that round's providers map, not in agents, and an extra key such as the migrated outcome block survives every append. (7) WHAT --record GAINS. When a ledger exists for the target, the record gains two keys — rounds_ledger (the repo-relative ledger path) and final_round (its round count) — and --record REFUSES, exit 2 with nothing written and any existing record left byte-identical, when the ledger's last round's reviewed_hash differs from the hash it is about to record. A record can only ever be the ledger's last round, so a record cannot be filed for content the ledger never saw. When no ledger exists --record behaves exactly as today and prints one notice line naming run_review.py --round, so the older two-step flow keeps working and says what it is missing. Nothing else about --record changes. (8) THE ONE HAND-WRITTEN LEDGER IS MIGRATED. .karta/roundtable/context-economy.rounds.json was written by hand before this mode existed and uses older names. It is normalized to the emitted shape — binder to target_ref, kind to target_kind, each round's staged_blob_sha256 to reviewed_hash, each round gaining below_floor: false — with every value preserved: thirteen rounds in order, the same hashes, the same findings text, the outcome block kept as an extra header key. One shape exists after this, so the gate and the page each read one. No other file under .karta/roundtable/ is touched. (9) SELF-TEST. Additions in the house pattern, each with a negative control: the first --round creates the ledger and the second extends it; a below-floor round is appended and flagged rather than refused; a verdict-less provider survives into the round; --check still fails for a target that has only a ledger; --record refuses on a hash mismatch and passes once a fresh round is appended; the header survives an append. The script reports 39/39 today; the oracle requires at least 55/55, all passing. (MIGRATION, CHECKED IN FULL) The migration may change exactly three header things — the `note` text (which today says the gate reads only the record, no longer true), and the `binder`/`kind` keys which become `target_ref`/`target_kind` — and may add keys (`tool`, `agents`, per-round `run_at`, `below_floor`); it must preserve every other committed value at every depth: all thirteen `reviewed_hash` values (renamed from staged_blob_sha256), every provider entry with its model, verdict and status, every findings string, every notes string, and the `outcome` block. The oracle walks the version committed at 4602ecf (the commit that holds the hand-written ledger — a fixed reference, so the check is the same before and after the migration lands and never a tautology) against the migrated file with that exact allowance, so a regenerated or garbled interior cannot pass. Every migrated round gains `below_floor: false` — each hand-written round carried two real verdicts — and the oracle asserts the value, not the key. (TARGET GRAMMAR AND SAFE WRITES) `--round` and `--record` accept a binder target only when it matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` (or resolves to such a slug from a binder path under .karta/binders/), and a branch target only when it resolves to a hex tip SHA; `..`, `/` in a slug, `\\`, a leading `~` or an absolute path are refused (exit 2, nothing written, nothing staged) — self-test negative controls for `../foo`, `a/b`, `/tmp/x`, `~x`. An EXISTING ledger that does not parse, has no or empty `rounds`, or whose last round lacks `reviewed_hash` makes both modes refuse (exit 2) and leave the file byte-identical — never reinitialise, never append onto a torn file; self-test corrupts the ledger between two rounds and asserts refusal plus byte identity. Ledger writes are atomic: temp file in the same directory, then rename. Every refusal — grammar, unresolvable target, torn ledger, rejected payload — exits 2 (one code, self-tested). The binder bytes hashed by --round/--record are read with a symlink check: a symlinked binder is refused (self-test). The same directory rule applies to writes: `--round` and `--record` refuse (exit 2, nothing written) when the resolved `.karta/roundtable` is not beneath the resolved repository root; self-test with a symlinked roundtable directory. The self-test and the oracle capture the full bytes of the existing record and ledger before a refused --record and assert both are byte-identical afterwards, and after EVERY successful --round assert the ledger is staged and the staged content equals the worktree ledger.

work_items.title: A plan cannot be committed unless its review rounds are committed with it
work_items.summary: With the new switch on, the commit gate and the merge gate each require the ledger alongside the record, and require its last round to have reviewed exactly the content being committed or merged.
work_items.contract: (1) THE SWITCH. .karta/roundtable.json gains one optional boolean, ledger. Absent or false, nothing about the gates changes — that default is what leaves consumer repos and every existing record alone until they opt in. This repo's own config sets "ledger": true in this item, which is what makes "the rounds are kept" a fact about the repo rather than a habit of whoever is at the keyboard. (2) THE VALIDATOR SHIPS IN THE SAME EDIT. scripts/validate_plugin.py rejects an unknown key in that config, so adding ledger to the file without adding it to the allow-list makes the repo's own floor command fail. Item 8 of check() gains ledger in the allowed-key tuple and a type check mirroring enabled's, with the error text `.karta/roundtable.json: 'ledger' must be a boolean`. The two edits are one change; the oracle proves it by running the whole validator over the committed config. (3) THE BINDER-COMMIT GATE. work_items.contract: (1) WHAT THE STATE CARRIES. current_state() gains one key per binder row, review, for every live and archived binder: null when neither .karta/roundtable/.json nor .karta/roundtable/.rounds.json exists; otherwise {record, rounds}, where record is {reviewed_hash, run_at, tool, panel} with panel a list of {provider, verdict} only, and rounds is the ledger's rounds array passed through unchanged, or null when there is no ledger. A binder with a record and no ledger — most of this repo's archived history — shows the record half and a null rounds half, which is what an unrecorded review history looks like and must not be dressed up as anything else. The record's panel prose is deliberately dropped: it is the full model responses, and it would ride every poll. The two files are found by convention from the slug, not through the record's rounds_ledger pointer, so a record written before that key existed still finds its ledger. (2) COST. Two file reads per binder per derivation and no git work at all: the read happens beside the binder load, and current_state() in this repository still makes exactly five subprocess.run calls — the count measured before this change — which the oracle asserts. The archived poll payload is untouched: _archived_entry still returns exactly {slug, total, done} and archived_entry_bound() is still 96, so an archived binder's strip comes from the load-time detail like the rest of its prose. Both are asserted, because a review block leaking into the compact entry would undo the shed-archived-payload win. The richest ledger in the repo serializes to 11,675 bytes of rounds today; the oracle holds one binder's whole review block under 32,768 bytes so growth is a decision someone makes rather than a poll that quietly widens. (3) WHAT THE PAGE SHOWS. Each binder card gains a review strip: how many rounds the plan took, each provider's final verdict, and one row per round carrying the round number, the first seven characters of the reviewed_hash it reviewed, one verdict pill per provider, and the counts of findings fixed and refuted; the findings text expands on click. A provider that returned nothing renders as a pill with no verdict carrying its status — the absence is shown, never omitted. A binder whose review is null renders no strip and no empty frame. (4) HOW IT IS BUILT. The page is the vendored global-build Vue Options-API app the karta-house-vue pack describes: the strip is a component registered on the same app with a string template, :key on the round rows is the round number, and the server-rendered HTML and _APP_JS render the same markup — the mirror rule the file already states. Test hooks data-kw-review-strip, data-kw-review-round and data-kw-review-verdict carry the data-kw- prefix already in use. (5) COVERAGE. Ten behaviours join the registry (the four named here plus the six added in clauses (6)–(9)) and the selftest_behaviours.txt anchor: review-strip-counts-the-rounds, review-round-row-names-its-blob-and-verdicts, review-strip-absent-when-no-review, review-detail-never-enters-the-archived-poll-entry — each with the negative controls the registry requires. The page reports 258/258 today; the oracle requires at least 270/270. (6) MIRRORS. serve_status.py and selftest_behaviours.txt are mirrored byte-identically into .agents/skills/karta-status/scripts/ and plugins/karta/skills/karta-status/scripts/; run `python3 scripts/sync_codex_skills.py` after the final canonical edit, and the oracle re-checks it. VERSION is not bumped — that is release work. (6) FINDINGS ARE TEXT, NEVER MARKUP. Ledger findings and notes are free prose written by an operator or a model; the strip renders them only through text interpolation (`{{ }}` / v-text) — never v-html — and the served page carries no `v-html` at all: the oracle renders the page through `render_app_html` with a state whose review block holds hostile values and asserts the literal `v-html` is absent from the served document OUTSIDE the inlined state (the state legitimately inlines binder text, including this binder's own contract, which mentions the literal — measured: 14 occurrences inside the inlined state today and 0 outside it; a whole-file source count would collide with the very self-test this item adds, so the pin is on served output). work_items.title: The operator guides explain how to read a ledger and the strip that shows it
work_items.summary: The roundtable guide gains a section that reads the thirteen-round context-economy ledger as its worked example, and the Karta Watch guide describes the review strip.
work_items.contract: Two prose edits, written last so they describe what actually landed. (1) docs/how-to/roundtable.md gains a section headed exactly '## Reading a ledger', after 'Recording a review'. It reads the real .karta/roundtable/context-economy.rounds.json as its worked example — thirteen rounds; the last round's hash equal to the binder blob the record beside it was filed against; one provider that returned nothing in every single round and is listed in every single round anyway — and names the keys a reader will meet: reviewed_hash, findings_fixed, findings_refuted_or_deferred, below_floor. It says plainly what the ledger is not: never a substitute for the record — the record stays authoritative for freshness and the floor, and with `ledger: true` the gate additionally requires the ledger's final round to have reviewed the same committed content the record identifies, not a verdict anyone is held to, and not a substitute for either. (2) docs/how-to/karta-watch.md gains a section headed exactly '## The review strip' describing what the card shows, where its two files come from, and that a binder reviewed before ledgers existed shows its record and no rounds. (3) Both follow the repo's plain-language rules and the minimum-separator table style, and neither explains the JSON key by key — these files are read by people using karta. This item depends on the other three because it is written from what landed, never from the plan. The section names the round-13 hash prefix 6d68c0e8, says plainly that one provider returned nothing in every round and why that is visible only in the ledger, and notes that a branch ledger is one ledger per tip sha (the multi-round history is a binder's), since the doc-truth probe checks pointers, not these claims. benchmarks/probes/parity-doc-truth-ledger.py is PRE-EXISTING and unchanged by this item — it is run, not written, which is why it is absent from touches.
